questions.question: The IUPAC nomenclature of the structure shown is

questions.explanation: The longest chain is butane and both substituents are on carbon 2. Bromo is cited before methyl alphabetically, giving 2-bromo-2-methylbutane.

questions.question: The IUPAC nomenclature of the compound shown is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the energy profile shown, y represents
questions.explanation: The arrow y measures the energy difference from reactants to the transition-state peak. This minimum energy barrier is the activation energy.
questions.topic: Chemical energetics — Energy changes in reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The table shows formulae of some ions. In which compound is the formula not correct?
questions.explanation: Iron(III) is Fe³⁺ while bromide is Br⁻. One iron ion needs three bromide ions, so the correct formula is FeBr₃, not Fe₃Br.
questions.topic: Chemical combination — Ionic compounds and formulae

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the equilibrium 2XY₃(g) ⇌ X₂(g) + 3Y₂(g), the expression for Kc is
questions.explanation: Kc is products over reactants, with each concentration raised to its stoichiometric coefficient. Thus Kc = [X₂][Y₂]³ / [XY₃]².

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction C₃H₈ + Cl₂ → C₃H₇Cl + HCl in ultraviolet light is
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet light initiates replacement of a hydrogen atom in propane by chlorine. This replacement of one atom or group by another is substitution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: From the solubility graph, it can be inferred that
options: the solubility of X and Y is the same at all temperatures
the solubility of X, Y and Z is temperature dependent
the solubility of Z increases as temperature increases
the solubility of Y increases steadily as temperature increases
questions.explanation: The line labelled Y rises steadily as temperature increases. It therefore shows a consistent increase in solubility with increasing temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the formula table, the two compounds that combine in the presence of an acid catalyst to produce compound V are
questions.explanation: Compound I is an alcohol, ROH, and IV is a carboxylic acid, RCOOH. They form the ester V, RCOOR′, by acid-catalysed esterification.
questions.topic: Organic chemistry — Carboxylic acids and esters
